summary: Ushta tower in Saskatchewan: a new cupola is recorded in the 1958 annual report, and Wenzel Fialkowski is listed there 1973-2002; no source describes the site today.

facts.agency: Saskatchewan Department of Natural Resources (named in the annual report cited on Canada Lookouts)
facts.status_note: No source we found says whether the tower still stands.

staffing.status: Wenzel Fialkowski listed at Ushta from 1973 to 2002 on the websiteservice.ca towermen list

events.note: New cupola on the Ushta tower, dated 1958 on Canada Lookouts and sourced to the Department of Natural Resources annual report for the year ending 31 March 1959.
Wenzel Fialkowski listed at Ushta from 1973.
Last year of the Fialkowski entry at Ushta on the towermen list.

evidence.supports: Position of Ushta on the tower list

evidence.quote: 1958: New construction during the year consisted of a new cupola on the Ushta tower.

evidence.supports: The annual report cited for the cupola is for the year ending 31 March 1959
evidence.quote: Department of Natural Resources Annual Report, FY ending 3/31/1959

evidence.supports: Wenzel Fialkowski listed at Ushta from 1973 to 2002, then went to aerial detection

sources.title: Firetowers of Saskatchewan: Firetowermen and Women

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Canada Lookouts files the cupola under 1958, but the annual report it quotes covers the year ending 31 March 1959. The story keeps both dates and does not choose between them.

notes_for_editor: Thin record: the tower-list entry gives coordinates only, with no height, build date, status or access. The towermen list's 'went to aerial detection' note is read as applying to Fialkowski after his 2002 entry. The 1958 brief event is kept; the annual report year is ambiguous (see resolved_conflicts). The brief's agency (Saskatchewan Public Safety Agency) is not named in any fetched source. Nothing fetched describes the site today, and no photos were found.
